title: The Lantern Wake
premise: Generations ago, Lantern Master Alden Vale was killed and the lantern he carried between the islands was corrupted. Each year he returned its light to Bellwether's shrine to renew the tide. Now the spreading darkness has reached the harbor. Ada, Ren, Iona and Tavi must recover the lantern from the ruined Tide Cistern, bring it home and begin restoring the other islands.

heroes.description: A harbor guard who would rather mend a shield than raise it.

heroes.name: Ren
heroes.description: A rope runner who knows every roof above the docks.

heroes.name: Iona
heroes.description: An apprentice healer who listens for the sea in empty shells.

heroes.name: Tavi
heroes.description: A lamp maker learning to turn a spark into a signal.

maps.name: Bellwether Harbor
maps.description: A stranded fishing harbor with an empty lantern shrine. Keeper Mara waits beside it; Orrin tends the western rest house. The northern path leads to Saltglass Causeway. Safe from encounters.

maps.name: Saltglass Causeway
maps.description: A weathered coastal route showing the spreading corruption. Supplies lie at the western camp below the ruined arch; Sable offers advice nearby. The south path returns to Bellwether and the northeast path reaches the Tide Cistern.

maps.name: The Tide Cistern
maps.description: A once peaceful beacon complex ruined by corrupted lantern light. Reach the northwest valve to drain the central crossing. Beyond it, the Hollow Bell guards Alden's lantern at the back of the beacon chamber. The southwest path returns to the causeway.

npcs.name: Keeper Mara
npcs.description: Bellwether's keeper, preserving the accounts of Alden Vale's lost journeys.

npcs.name: Orrin
npcs.description: A patient ferryman keeping the rest house open.

npcs.name: Sable
npcs.description: A retired keeper who tends the causeway camp and remembers the islands' warnings.

lines: Every island has its own shrine, but Alden's lantern linked their lights. One harbor's hope belongs to all of them.
Whatever lies ahead, remember this: keepers bring the light home, and then carry it onward.
This wheel controls the center channel. Turning it will drain the water and reveal the crossing to the beacon chamber.
The channel is draining. We have a way through to the lantern.
The tide has stopped. Our boats are stranded, and the shrine stands empty.
Generations ago, Lantern Master Alden Vale carried one lantern between the islands. Each year he brought it home to this shrine to renew our tide.
Alden was killed. No one knows by whom. His lantern never returned, and its corrupted light has spread from island to island. Now it has reached Bellwether.
The old records place the lantern in the ruined Tide Cistern, beyond Saltglass Causeway. Its guardian, the Hollow Bell, has been corrupted too.
Find the lantern and bring it back to me at the harbor shrine. If we can wake its true light, Bellwether's tide may return.
Alden's route once brought travelers from every island. Now even the ferries are stranded.
Check your supplies before you set out. You can always return here; no crew should face the sea exhausted.
The corruption crossed the islands long before our tide failed. Those withered roots are its warning.
A keeper learns more than one craft. Open Jobs to prepare your crew for the cistern's guardians.
Try water magic against wick moths. The silt guards are tougher to handle with fists alone.
There are salves in the supply chest beside this camp. Take them before heading northeast to the cistern.
The old beacon should have guided people safely home. Something has twisted it into a prison.
The northwest sluice controls the central crossing. Beyond it waits the corrupted guardian.
Check our equipment and supplies before we face the guardian. We go together.
The Hollow Bell is still. Its duty was to protect the lantern, but the corruption turned it against everyone who came near.
Here is Alden's lantern. There is a small, warm light beneath the dark glass. We can carry it home.
The guardian cannot tell us who killed him. That mystery is still out there.
Bring the lantern to Mara at Bellwether's shrine. Its true light may answer there.
Set Alden's lantern in the shrine. After all these generations, its light has come home.
Look! The flame is warming, and the water is moving again. Bellwether's tide is returning.
But the other islands are still caught in the corruption. When you are ready, carry this light to their shrines as Alden once did.
We still do not know who killed him. For now, you have given Bellwether a tomorrow. This is where your journey begins.
